script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - DAY

CRAIG, 16, lanky and glasses, watches a PICKUP GAME of basketball with a mixture of awe and longing. He's never been part of a team before, always the outsider.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
Craig wanted to belong. To be a part of something.

Suddenly, a stray basketball comes flying toward him. He catches it, surprised. The team, led by JASON, a popular senior, notices.

JASON
(smiling)
Not bad, Freshman.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL CAFE - DAY

Craig approaches JASON at lunch, nervous.

CRAIG
Hey, I was wondering if you wanted to practice with me sometime?

JASON
(raising an eyebrow)
You mean, like, one-on-one?

CRAIG
Yeah, I just... I want to get better.

JASON
(grinning)
Alright, sure. Tomorrow after school?

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - AFTERNOON

Craig arrives early for practice. He's eager and determined.

JASON enters, followed by the rest of the team: MIKE, a muscular sophomore; LUCAS, a quiet junior; and EMMA, a talented senior.

They begin to practice, and Craig struggles at first. But the team is patient and encouraging.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - EVENING

After weeks of practice, the team starts to gel. They share jokes and stories, and Craig feels like he finally belongs.

EMMA
(smiling at Craig)
You've really improved.

MIKE
Yeah, you're starting to get the hang of it.

LUCAS
(patting Craig on the back)
Keep it up.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - NIGHT

The team enters the gym for their first official game. They're up against the school's powerhouse team, The Titans. The pressure is high.

CRAIG
(whispering to Jason)
We can do this.

JASON
(smiling)
We've got this.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - DURING THE GAME

The game is intense. Craig plays better than ever before, and the team follows suit. They're in sync, a well-oiled machine.

Suddenly, the opposing team's star player, TYSON, makes a move for the ball. Craig blocks him, but Tyson retaliates, pushing Craig to the ground.

The referees blow their whistles, but instead of fighting back, Craig looks up at his teammates. They all rush to his side, forming a protective barrier around him.

The crowd goes wild. The team has proven their strength not just in their skills on the court, but in their unbreakable bond.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
